correctness.rationale: The recursive root/component decomposition enumerates each rooted elimination tree exactly once. The seven proper descendant tubes characterize maximal tubings, while deleting one tube leaves a ridge with two completions; their pair constitutes exactly one allowed single flip. A separate parent–child rotation interpretation agrees with these moves in the source. For each graph the independent C++ audit built induced-component elimination trees, tubes, ridge-pair adjacency, tested all 8!=40,320 candidate label permutations to get full automorphism groups, enumerated every orbit, and ran breadth-first search from each orbit representative across all states. It reconstructed Q3 16,752 states, 58,632 edges, 48 base automorphisms, 355 state-orbits (343×48+12×24), and M8 17,568 states, 61,488 edges, 16 automorphisms, 1,098 state-orbits; eccentricity distributions Q3 {17:1368,18:8280,19:6336,20:768}, M8 {17:976,18:5536,19:10800,20:256}, and all twenty pair distances matched the frozen theorem. Orbit multiplicity and division of ordered pair counts by two ensure entire distance distributions, not samples; connected BFS reaches all states. This is a genuinely exhaustive finite proof of the two specified graphs, not numerical extrapolation to other graphs.

value.rationale: Q3 and M8 are canonical contrasting connected cubic graphs of order eight. Their rotation graphs attain the same radius/diameter yet sharply different antipodal multiplicities and complete distance distributions. This isolates a natural limitation of diameter alone as a descriptor of graph-associahedron geometry, provides reproducible complete finite metric data, and supplies test cases for more general rotation-distance algorithms and heuristics. A finite census can be valuable on these canonical inputs without a general theorem.
